newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal - Basis firm on supply, China.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal - Basis firm on supply, China.

text.p: Rail soymeal offers in some cash markets were higher Thursday and movement was slow as supplies of spot soymeal remained tight and end-users waited for the CBOT October contract to expire, cash brokers said.
"Right now, December looks too cheap, so they might as well wait until next week to buy," said one Kentucky dealer.
Some dealers are looking for soymeal basis levels to slip next week as supplies from last week's larger-than-expected U.S. soybean crush hit the market.
On Thursday, the National Oilseed Processors Association reported a weekly crushing pace of 27.89 million bushels. The total was up from 25,42 million a week earlier and 27.0 million a year earlier.

Brisk soymeal exports were also seen keeping basis levels firm, dealers said. On Friday morning, the U.S. Department of Agriculture reported weekly export sales of 167,000 tonnes of meal to China during the week ended October 10.
"The demand out of China along is going to keep us in pretty good shape," one soymeal broker said.
